title: Safe motor start-stop
summary: Walk through a motor with seal-in, stop, and overload handling using the Motor Start Stop example.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Hold the motor on after Start is released with a seal-in.
Drop the motor out on Stop, EStop and Overload, and never let a held Start restart it by itself.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Motor.st, replace Forward := Start with a seal-in built from Start, Stop, EStop, and Overload; verify that Reverse remains FALSE.
stages.checkpoint: Forward stays ON after Start is released and drops on Stop, EStop, or Overload.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict Motor.Forward at {{t:0}}, {{t:20}}, {{t:40}}, {{t:50}}, {{t:90}}, and {{t:140}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: OFF at {{t:0}} ms even though Start is held; ON at {{t:20}}; OFF at {{t:40}} (EStop) and still OFF at {{t:50}} while Start is held; OFF at {{t:90}} (Overload) and {{t:140}} (Stop). It turns ON again only after Start is released and pressed again, at {{t:70}}, {{t:120}}, and {{t:170}} ms. Motor.Reverse remains OFF.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program copies Start to Forward, so the motor runs only while Start is held. Change it so that Forward stays ON after a press of Start, goes OFF on Stop, EStop and Overload, and turns ON again only after Start has been released and pressed again, also when the program starts with Start held. Reverse stays FALSE. Write the statements yourself, and declare the memories you need.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named MotorStartStop and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare the trace: EStop at {{t:40}} ms, overload at {{t:90}} ms, and stop at {{t:140}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: EStop, Overload, and Stop force Motor.Forward OFF, and holding Start does not restart it.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: At {{t:50}} ms EStop is released while Start is still held. Why must the motor stay OFF there, and what would an operator in front of the machine expect?
stages.checkpoint: A motor that starts by itself when a stop ends surprises the people near it. After any stop, a start needs a new press of Start.

hints.text: The output has to remember that Start was pressed: keep a memory variable that Start sets and that holds itself until a stop condition clears it.
Clear the memory first when Stop, EStop or Overload is TRUE; only then let Start set it, and only if Start was seen released since the last stop, so a held Start cannot restart the motor.

faultCases: The starting program copies Start to Forward, so the motor runs only while Start is held.
